title: observability: token-kv metrics + dashboard enhancements and alert tuning
author: Elena Rodriguez
description: Add token-level KV cache metrics, a dedicated token-KV dashboard, and tuned alerts for sustained KV-miss driven cost regressions. Motivation: recent incidents and canary data showed undetected regressions in per-token KV cache behavior causing both latency and cost spikes for multi-turn chat routes. This PR introduces server-side metrics (token_kv_hits_total, token_kv_misses_total, token_kv_hit_ratio, token_kv_latency_seconds_bucket) instrumented per-model and per-route, a prebuilt Grafana dashboard that breaks down token-level cost and latency by KV hit/miss, and updated alert rules that detect sustained drops in hit ratio and sudden increases in per-token latency or cost. Changes summary: 1) observability/metrics: add KV metrics and labels for model_id, route, customer_tier; 2) observability/dashboards: new token_kv_dashboard with panels for hit ratio, per-token cost, latency percentiles, and capacity heatmap; 3) alerts: tuned thresholds with rolling-window evaluation and rate-limited paged alerts; 4) docs: add observability/kv_metrics.md describing metric semantics and recommended dashboards/Runbook; 5) tests: unit and integration tests for metric emission and dashboard schema validation. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag `obs.token_kv_metrics` with gradual ramp to 50% of traffic for 48h, watch canary dashboards, then full rollout. Related work: ENG-4021 (kv cache observability epic), ENG-4088 (alarming platform improvements), PM-501 (dashboard requirements). Checklist: - [x] Add metrics and expose in prometheus format - [x] Dashboard panels and variables added - [x] Alerts tuned with runbook links - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Docs updated - [x] Feature flag and phased rollout plan Tests: unit tests for new counters, integration test validating label cardinality bounds, end-to-end dashboard validate job. Migration notes: metric names are additive; no consumer break expected. Observability owners: @Aditi @Marcus. Contact on-call if alerts fire during rollout.
